### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **107** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md`, `packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**59** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/liveness/object.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/object.md`, `packages/spec/src/data/user-action-transfer.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `enforceAuth (32 routes)`, `resolveExecCtx (37 routes)`, `routeManager (26 routes)`, `enforceApiAccess (12 routes)`, `resolveProtocol (29 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 56 pages)`, `/data/:object/:id (route, 38 pages)`
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **189** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `7e50969e5f9c1727ddb0fcc9418c646f89050c18` — the merge of head `8ecad2fc6844118c2e6c5004b73b024f25f1855e` into base `1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7e50969e5f9c1727ddb0fcc9418c646f89050c18 && git checkout 7e50969e5f9c1727ddb0fcc9418c646f89050c18
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b 8ecad2fc6844118c2e6c5004b73b024f25f1855e && git checkout -B drift-repro 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b && git merge --no-ff 8ecad2fc6844118c2e6c5004b73b024f25f1855e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1705ec955c2097933a0a0776e9c00d270c26907b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

repo:objectstack#4 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5nbzs5iP1HcMCFhZo5

**L1 verdict (L1-a): REWORK, two items** at head `a8787f4282c173e3e35bfadb40e46557a562de64` (Fixes #35402, seat note 7065223271). Full read of `origin/main...a8787f4282` (28 files, +1592/−43).

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.**
- `l1-face --pr 36154` at a8787f4282 is CLEAN (13 items):
  - First line `Fixes #35402`.
  - `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: the new code, the two routes and the client methods are named in the body.
  - Floors are success.
  - Check-runs: 60 success, 10 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.
- One changeset covers all five touched published packages: core, rest, client, spec and service-messaging.
- The body's local runs are on `06b053c2`. The later commits are a doubles/test fix (`0823c1f730`), merges of main, and a liveness count-shard regeneration. CI at the head covers them.

**What reads right.**
- **Order of checks** (`change-record-owner.ts`):
  1. Body and closed-set checks.
  2. Then the switch, via `changeOwnerOffReason`, which runs `resolveUserActionTransfer` and refuses `403 CHANGE_OWNER_DISABLED` before any record read, whoever asks.
  3. Then the target, via `assertAssignableUser`. This is a byte-faithful extraction of the hand-over's own check.
  4. Then one by-id `engine.update` per row under the caller's context.
  - So the transfer verdict is the owner guard's, with no second permission check. That matches ruling 7000907189 point 2 and the card's "per-row by-id updates under the caller's context".
- **The change set.** It is `{ owner_id }`, or `{ owner_id: null, queue }` for a queue target. A queue target on an object without a `queue` column is refused `400`.
- **The bulk form.**
  - The #30205 shape and `USER_WORK_TRANSFER_ROW_CAP` are reused.
  - Empty, over-cap and duplicate ids are refused before any write.
  - Every failed row is listed with the door's own code, through `rowFailureAnswer`, which uses the same classifier as the single door.
- **Refusal envelope** (`change-owner-routes.ts`). `UserWorkTransferRefusal` answers its status and code with `details.fields`. Everything else goes through `handleRouteError` into `nestedRefusalEnvelope`. The rest tests pin each refusal by status and code.
- **Done-when.** Every row of the body's table has a pin:
  - off and ineligible objects, for single and bulk, with a `modifyAllRecords` holder in dogfood;
  - edit without transfer, `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`;
  - the mixed bulk report;
  - the queue target;
  - notify.
- **The MEASURED case is real.** On the showcase's `private` note, after alice hands it to bob:
  - `created_by` stays alice;
  - bob gets `GET` 200 and `PATCH` 200;
  - alice gets `GET` 404 and `PATCH` 404.
- **Spec.**
  - The `CHANGE_OWNER_DISABLED` ledger row is filed under `@objectstack/core`, the stamping package, which is what the provenance gate requires. The seat note said `@objectstack/rest`, and the body explains why it differs.
  - The `userActions.transfer` liveness row goes from `planned` to `live`, with the `authorWarn`/`authorHint` dropped in the same edit, as its own note asked.
  - The two docblocks are prose only.
  - `git grep` finds no `content/docs` or `skills/**` page left saying "nothing reads it yet".

**R1 (should-fix, or name a follow-up #N in the body). The notification is English-only.** `notifyNewOwner` sends a literal `payload.title` ("A … record was assigned to you" / "N … records were assigned to you"), built from the object's untranslated `label`. Nothing lets it render in the new owner's language. The platform's own notices do:
- `service-messaging`'s `slack-links.ts` sends `keyedText: { titleKey, bodyKey, params }` beside the English literal, and the dispatcher renders it per recipient (#24978).
- `plugin-audit`'s mention notice resolves the recipient's locale before it builds its title.

Either carry `keyedText` (a `messages.*` key with `{ label, count }` params in the message bundles) and widen `ChangeOwnerMessaging.emit` to pass it, or leave it out and file a follow-up card, naming it in the body. Which one is the seat's call. It changes no ruling.

**R2 (must fix: a refusal without its code).** `change-owner-endpoint.dogfood.test.ts`, in the queue case: carol's refused queue move asserts only `status 403`. Pin the code too (the data door's `PERMISSION_DENIED`, as the edit-without-transfer case does). Otherwise a refusal for any other reason passes this pin.

**N1 (nit, non-blocking).** The dogfood notify case is titled "gets one inbox notification naming the record", but it asserts `sys_notification` rows by topic `>= 1`. It does not check that the row is bob's, that it is one, or that it names the record. Narrowing the query to bob and `source_id` would make the title true.

**Next.**
- R1, by a commit or a follow-up #N in the body.
- R2, by a test commit.
- I will read only that delta.
- After ACCEPT, the contract record is the seat's.

## Contract review
Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a8787f4282c173e3e35bfadb40e46557a562de64`
Local-runs: probe — ran the PR's own core and rest suites on the head to confirm the refusal pins hold against freshly built `core` and `spec` dists.
Scope: full diff of merge base `1f11c33d56..a8787f42` (28 files); read in full `packages/core/src/security/change-record-owner.ts`, `packages/rest/src/change-owner-routes.ts`, both unit suites, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/change-owner-endpoint.dogfood.test.ts`, the `user-assigned-work.ts`, `rest-server.ts`, `rest-route-ledger.ts`, client, spec, liveness, changeset and messaging hunks; read for context `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:1816-2140` (owner guard), `packages/objectql/src/engine-referential-integrity.ts:176-345,376-392` (reference check), `packages/metadata-core/src/engine-update-dispatch.ts:428-473`, `packages/rest/src/user-work-routes.ts`, `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`; card #35402 with all comments, order-35402.md, PR body, final-head declaration 7068380984, siblings #35403 and #35399.
Security-touching: yes

### ① Derived judgments

- **Object switch.** `offeredDefinition` (`change-record-owner.ts:178-191`) runs first in both forms (`:261`, `:306`) and throws `403 CHANGE_OWNER_DISABLED` from `resolveUserActionTransfer` before any read or write. It takes no caller input, so a `modifyAllRecords` holder is refused like anyone else. Holds.
- **Per-record permission.** Each row is one `engine.update(object, changeSet, { where: { id }, context })` under the caller's context (`:263`, `:323`). A pure-id `where` dispatches by-id (`engine-update-dispatch.ts:438-473`), so the row meets the edit pre-image gate and the owner guard at step 3.5 (`security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts:2031-2137`): transfer grant, or the ADR-0142 claim / release, else `PERMISSION_DENIED`. No second permission rule is written in the endpoint, and none is missing. Holds, single and bulk, every row.
- **Record existence.** A row the caller cannot reach and a row that does not exist answer the same thing on each branch (the caller-context pre-image is `null` for both, `:2043-2057`; the update returns nothing for both, `change-record-owner.ts:264-266`). The door answers what `PATCH /data/:object/:id` answers. Holds.
- **Tenant wall.** The target probe spreads the caller's context before `isSystem` (`user-assigned-work.ts:303`), so `tenantId` reaches the driver; the per-row write also runs the ordinary reference check on `owner_id`. No cross-organization write is admitted.
- **Target user.** See F1: the target pre-check does not ask the caller's read door. No write is admitted by it (the per-row reference check still refuses), so this is a disclosure finding, not a write hole.
- **System callers.** The HTTP door refuses an anonymous caller (`change-owner-routes.ts:221,255`) and passes the resolved caller context only. An in-process `isSystem` caller of the core functions still meets the switch and the target check; it bypasses the permission layer as any engine write does.
- **Bulk.** Cap is `USER_WORK_TRANSFER_ROW_CAP` (500), refused not truncated (`:291-298`); empty and repeated ids refused before any write (`:292-305`); per-row failure with id, code and sentence (`:329-332`); partial success, not transactional, as declared; hooks, validation, sharing recompute and audit fire as on a hand edit because each row is an ordinary update.
- **Spec.** `object.zod.ts` and `user-action-transfer.ts` hunks are docblock prose only; `error-code-ledger.zod.ts:1194-1204` adds one member; liveness flips `transfer` from `planned` to `live` and drops the author warning. No published schema shape changes. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right: nothing narrows. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. `patch` on all five packages follows the level rule for kind `none`.
- **Envelope and ledger.** Both rows are in `rest-route-ledger.ts:386-389` (`data-actions`, sdk); refusals go through `sendError` in the nested envelope (`change-owner-routes.ts:196-208`); route-envelope ratchet row at 0/0/0.
- **Pins.** Removing the switch check fails core `change-record-owner.test.ts:96`, rest `change-owner-routes.test.ts:107,229` and dogfood `:94`. The transfer check lives in plugin-security, not in this diff; removing it fails dogfood `:85`, `:144-151`, `:160-163`, which run the real `SecurityPlugin`. The admit path is dogfood `:107-129`.
- **Runs.** core `change-record-owner.test.ts` 21/21. rest `change-owner-routes.test.ts` 14/14 after rebuilding the local `core` and `spec` dists from the head; before the rebuild the stale dists gave 10 then 2 failures (missing export, then the unregistered code normalised to `PERMISSION_DENIED`), which is this checkout's state, not the PR's. Dogfood not run here (needs the closure build); CI on the head is the authority for it.

### ② Declarations

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: confirmed. New code `CHANGE_OWNER_DISABLED` (403), the two routes, `data.changeOwner` / `data.changeOwnerMany`, and the new `@objectstack/core` exports.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: confirmed.
- Ledger key: the seat note 7065223271 named `@objectstack/rest`; the PR registers the code under `@objectstack/core` because core stamps it and the provenance gate keys on the stamping package. Declared in the PR body; accepted.
- Changeset levels: `patch` ×5, confirmed.

### ③ Findings

- **F1 · should-fix · SECURITY.** The new-owner pre-check (`packages/core/src/security/user-assigned-work.ts:297-316`, called at `change-record-owner.ts:201-203,262,307`) does not follow the rule the write path's reference check follows for a user the caller cannot read (`engine-referential-integrity.ts:322-327`, #29029). Details are with the seat, not on this record. Fix in the shared function so both of its doors follow the write path's rule, correct its docblock (`:293-295`), and pin it.
- **F2 · should-fix.** `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx` lists every `/data` route, `:id/clone` and its `CLONE_DISABLED` included (`:433-441`), and has no entry for the two Change Owner routes, their bodies, the 500 cap, the per-row report or `CHANGE_OWNER_DISABLED`. A declared Clause-② surface lands undocumented on the page that enumerates that surface.
- **N1 · nit.** A change to the record's current owner is admitted as an echo and counted in `updated`; with `notify: true` the current owner is told the record "was assigned" to them (`change-record-owner.ts:327-338`, `:268-270`).
- **N2 · nit.** The two ledger rows carry no `responseSchema` (`rest-route-ledger.ts:386-387`), and the client's `ChangeOwnerResult` / `ChangeOwnerReport` are hand copies of core's types (`packages/client/src/index.ts:299-321`).
- **N3 · nit.** No pin for a transfer-grant holder on a record it can read but not edit through this door; the gate is the middleware's and is pinned on the PATCH door.

### ④ Accepted deviations

- None. F1 and F2 are open.
